description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities . Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the grant award letter, the dates for submission of the annual reports are mentioned. In case of a three-year project, between 5-7 reports are obligatory. The first report (0) is a very short report which focuses on specific conditions and/or recommendations in the grant. There is no need to report on progress in achieving outputs and outcomes, which is done in the first annual report. As annex to the report 0, the consortium agreements between the partners should be submitted. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

title.narrative: 2. Project progress and achievement

description.narrative: In this section (maximum 1000 words), please provide a global overview of the project progress **per output**. To what extent have they been achieved? Comment on the activities that have taken place and the most important milestones.

actual.value:
Overall, working in Kinshasa was complex for both participants and trainers due to the unsafe situation in the city, the lack of hygiene, the hopeless infrastructure (traffic jams), the lawlessness and the daily struggle for a living.
When there are so few opportunities for talented young people, it is tough to keep believing in yourself. Pedagogy and didactics focused on discipline, responsibility and 'together we are stronger' weighed heavily in the training. What is the point of ploughing through the mud and being on time every day when prospects are minimal, elections are sold in advance and family is panicking to survive a living. Nevertheless, the training team took the participants on a journey where achievement and progression were visible to them on a daily basis. The feeling of others putting energy, time and knowledge into them was heartening through which all participants flourished.
The teamwork found its strength in the realisation of a final performance in which they could express their own stories and desire for a better world for themselves and others. A performance that showed them who they themselves are and how complicated their environment is. An analysis they take away next to the strong technical progression and enrichment in expression possibilities. Never before they saw how they could use verbal and physical language to tell a story that gave them and an audience space to reflect on themselves and how they want to move forward. For them, telling a story with dance and theater became a wonderfully inspiring and educational experience. The seed of self-activation and self-confidence was planted. A momentum from which they can move forward. This is the most important milestone.
All outputs have been realised:
**1. Training in SRHR and specific GBV**
The three-day training by Afia Mama, an SRHR organisation supported by the Dutch Embassy, had a strong impact on the participants. Beforehand, every participant assumed that gender was not really an issue. Mrs Modi, Congolese, used simple examples to demonstrate that there is still a lot of prejudice towards women, that there is little mutual responsibility and that the women in the group are often not aware of this either. As one of the participants said: 'I learned that as a human being I have my rights but also my duties'. The training was active and often confrontational. It was not easy to accept that the artistic leader of Likit'Arts defended the right to correct his wife physically. Especially because on social media he bragged about his gender sensitivity. This brought unrest amongst participants and trainers .After this module, nonetheless a positive change was observed in the relationship between participants and the women in particular were more empowered. The relation between participants and trainers with the artistic director reamined complicated.
**2. Training in cultural entrepreneurship**
The five-day training was for the 4 core members of Likit Arts as well as 16 other cultural entrepreneurs in Kinshasa. Dr Eric Loembet focused particularly on knowledge about project coordination , good governance and management of projects. He also spent a lot of time on the position and importance in cooperation between different partners in a project that are sometimes not sufficiently considered . On all subjects, participants were very enthusiastic about the training (score 5 out of a scale of 1-5) A large number of participants felt that their ideas about good project management had been radically changed.
**3.Basic/Intermediate contemporary dance training**
Four different contemporary dance techniques were trained by four different trainers. Ground technique, basic warm-up exercises, technique with 'flow and release', with resistance and relaxation, with emphasis on breathing, with the 'nine points spatial system'. From the Evaluation Report:"At the beginning, I felt heavy. I had trouble performing movements, the different exercises from each trainer, but now I feel good in my body , flexible thanks to the ground technique, the nine points clarity of space use, breathing, relaxation and resistance"
**4.Basic/Intermediate Urban and African dance techniques**
This training used various African dance techniques in a fusion with hip-hop (urban). Working with the four elements (water, fire, wind and earth) within the movement styles also enriched the phrasing,dynamics and colour of dance and performativity. ER:" Working with these four elements allowed me to personally identify with the way I dance and vary in the moment."
**5. Basic Acting and performance skills training**
This training particularly focused on self-actualisation , own power and many circle exercises to find energy together and feed each other. One of the most important parts of the training that made the group more a group and also stronger as individuals. We also worked with masks, use of written text and text interpretation and breathing. ER: "This workshop made me realise that a performance can combine dance and theatre. I learnt about facial expression, movements in space, acting, teamwork and solidarity".
**6. Improvisation/composition/Choreography training**
Nine point system, working with the four elements and intensive contact improvisation formed the basis of this training module. Among all respondents, these elements came back as instructive and brought a change in attitude and mental concentration. ER: "Contact work was completely new to me. It enabled me to be more sensitive, it strengthened my concentration on and awareness of another person in space; I could be lifted into the air, become light, it opened me up".
**7. Creating a performance based on gender and sexual rights**
Based on interviews, conversations, analyses and physical assignments, a number of social constraints have emerged that the group of young people see as inhibiting their development and that of their country. These issues were transformed into powerful scenes that made the audience aware of social constraints in a performance lasting almost an hour. Among other topics, reproductive health, abortion and child prostitution were SRHR themes and the lack of security, solidarity, lawlessness and lack of responsibility were themes falling under Rule of Law. ER:"This training made me realise that a performance can combine dance and theatre, and that dance in a performance can work as a language." "The method Feri de Geus used to create and arrange stories in movement stories inspired beautiful composition and brought us a lot of creativity." "This training is the best training I have done since I started my artist career".
"This programme has awaken in us a creative spirit, and to observe to listen and to learn and to reproduce and above all to live in harmony with each other."

title.narrative: B.I.6. Number of stimulating measures/extra facilities aimed at preparation, supervision and aftercare of female candidates

comment.narrative: 18-04-2024: The group of women was quite divers. Apaert from the person with albinism there were more matured women and rather young women (20 years old) in the training. Especially the younger women were not used to the discipline of being present as a matter of course. To create an equal situation for everyone and to give a sense of urgency and discipline to the training, the small allowance for transportation and personal spending was only given out if one was present on time or at the latest within an hour of starting. Lunch and water were always provided for everyone. At first this led to protests but over time the youngest in particular were also on time. Togetherness was worked on, the feeling of being able to achieve more together than alone. Solidarity and the feeling of being of service to others. A sense of responsibility was also fostered with strict attendance. An appgroup was installed for this purpose. even after the training, the coordinator of Le Grand Cru always motivated the young women to take responsibility and to report any absence in advance. There was a lot of training on the feeling of togetherness because outside the training room the feeling of disenfranchisement, insecurity threw everyone back on themselves.

title.narrative: B.I.12. Improved gender equality and gender awareness in the workplace

actual.value:
The gender neutral approach in the training has made everyone aware of the equal opportunities for all. The specific gender training by AFFIA MAMA , a Dutch supported NGO for women's rights, has strengthened this awareness. The training had its focus not only on women's rights but also addressed men's prejudices towards women and women's behaviour. For example, is a man allowed to cry and why is a man not allowed to hit his wife. Combined with a majority of female trainers, these role examples worked positively on all women but also on all men in the group, who became aware of the knowledge and power of female trainers.
